title: द्विचत्वारिंशत्तमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 42 · Arjuna and Ashvatthaman, and Yudhishthira's fall

summary.en: The Kurus and Srinjayas meet again under Yudhishthira, and Dhrishtadyumna rushes at Karna, enraged. Krishna speeds the chariot after Yudhishthira's words, and Arjuna turns toward the king.
summary.kn: ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರನ ನೇತೃತ್ವದಲ್ಲಿ ಕುರು, ಸೃಂಜಯರು ಮತ್ತೆ ಸಂಧಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಧೃಷ್ಟದ್ಯುಮ್ನ ಕೆರಳಿ ಕರ್ಣನ ಮೇಲೆ ಎರಗುತ್ತಾನೆ. ಯುಧಿಷ್ಠಿರನ ಮಾತಿನ ನಂತರ ಕೃಷ್ಣ ರಥ ವೇಗಗೊಳಿಸುತ್ತಾನೆ; ಅರ್ಜುನ ರಾಜನತ್ತ ತಿರುಗುತ್ತಾನೆ.
summary.hi: युधिष्ठिर के नेतृत्व में कुरु और सृंजय फिर मिलते हैं, और धृष्टद्युम्न क्रुद्ध होकर कर्ण पर टूटते हैं। युधिष्ठिर के वचनों के बाद कृष्ण रथ तेज़ करते हैं और अर्जुन राजा की ओर मुड़ते हैं।
summary.te: యుధిష్ఠిరుని నాయకత్వంలో కురు సృంజయులు మళ్లీ కలుస్తారు; ధృష్టద్యుమ్నుడు కోపంతో కర్ణునిపై దూకుతాడు. యుధిష్ఠిరుని మాటల తరువాత కృష్ణుడు రథాన్ని వేగవంతం చేస్తాడు; అర్జునుడు రాజు వైపు తిరుగుతాడు.
summary.ta: யுதிஷ்டிரர் தலைமையில் குருக்களும் சிருஞ்சயரும் மீண்டும் சந்திக்க, த்ருஷ்டத்யும்னன் சினத்துடன் கர்ணனைத் தாக்குகிறான். யுதிஷ்டிரரின் சொற்களுக்குப்பின் கண்ணன் தேரை விரைவுபடுத்த, அர்ஜுனன் மன்னரை நோக்கித் திரும்புகிறான்.
summary.ml: യുധിഷ്ഠിരന്റെ നേതൃത്വത്തിൽ കുരുക്കളും സൃഞ്ജയരും വീണ്ടും ഏറ്റുമുട്ടുന്നു; ധൃഷ്ടദ്യുമ്നൻ കോപത്തോടെ കർണ്ണനുനേരെ പായുന്നു. യുധിഷ്ഠിരന്റെ വാക്കുകൾക്കുശേഷം കൃഷ്ണൻ രഥം വേഗത്തിൽ തെളിക്കുന്നു; അർജുനൻ രാജാവിന്റെ നേർക്ക് തിരിയുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 8.42; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 29 2019

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
ततः पुनः समाजग्मुरभीताः कुरुसृञ्जयाः ।
युधिष्ठिरमुखाः पार्था वैकर्तनमुखा वयम् ॥

meaning.en: Then the fearless Kurus and Srinjayas came together again, the Pandavas led by Yudhishthira and we led by Karna, son of Vikartana.

verses.text:
ततः प्रववृते भीमः संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः ।
कर्णस्य पाण्डवानां च यमराष्ट्रविवर्धनः ॥

meaning.en: Then a terrible, hair-raising battle began between Karna and the Pandavas, one that swelled the realm of Yama.

verses.text:
तस्मिन्प्रवृत्ते संग्रामे तुमुले शोणितोदके ।
संशप्तकेषु शूरेषु किंचिच्छिष्टेषु भारत ॥

meaning.en: Bharata, as that tumultuous battle with its waters of blood went on, and only a few of the heroic Samshaptakas were left,

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नो महाराज सहितः सर्वराजभिः ।
कर्णमेवाभिदुद्राव पाण्डवाश्च महारथाः ॥

meaning.en: great king, Dhrishtadyumna with all the kings, and the Pandava great chariot-warriors, rushed at Karna alone.

verses.text:
आगच्छमानांस्तान्संख्ये प्रहृष्टान्विजयैषिणः ।
दधारैको रणे कर्णो जलौघानिव पर्वतः ॥

meaning.en: As they came on in the battle, joyful and eager for victory, Karna alone held them back, as a mountain holds back floods of water.

verses.text:
तमासाद्य तु ते कर्णं व्यशीर्यन्त महारथाः ।
यथाचलं समासाद्य जलौघाः सर्वतोदिशम् ।
तयोरासीन्महाराज संग्रामो लोमहर्षणः ॥

meaning.en: Reaching Karna, those great chariot-warriors were scattered, as floods of water are scattered in all directions on reaching a mountain. Great king, a hair-raising battle took place between them.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नस्तु राधेयं शरेण नतपर्वणा ।
ताडयामास संक्रुद्धस्तिष्ठ तिष्ठेति चाब्रवीत् ॥

meaning.en: Dhrishtadyumna, enraged, struck Radheya with an arrow with bent joints and said, "Stand, stand!"

verses.text:
विजयं तु धनुःश्रेष्ठं विधुन्वानो महारथः ।
पार्षतस्य धनुश्छित्त्वा शरानाशीविषोपमान् ।
ताडयामास संक्रुद्धः पार्षतं नवभिः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: The great chariot-warrior Karna, shaking his best of bows, Vijaya, cut the bow of the son of Prishata, and in anger struck him with nine arrows like venomous snakes.

verses.text:
ते वर्म हेमविकृतं भित्त्वा तस्य महात्मनः ।
शोणिताक्ता व्यराजन्त शक्रगोपा इवानघ ॥

meaning.en: Blameless one, those arrows pierced that great-souled man's gold-wrought armour and, smeared with blood, shone like red velvet mites.

verses.text:
तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नं धृष्टद्युम्नो महारथः ।
अन्यद्धनुरुपादाय शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान् ।
कर्णं विव्याध सप्तत्या शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ॥

meaning.en: Throwing aside that cut bow, the great chariot-warrior Dhrishtadyumna took another bow and arrows like venomous snakes, and pierced Karna with seventy arrows with bent joints.

verses.text:
तथैव राजन्कर्णोऽपि पार्षतं शत्रुतापनम् ।
द्रोणशत्रुं महेष्वासो विव्याध निशितैः शरैः ॥

meaning.en: In the same way, king, Karna, the great archer, pierced the son of Prishata, tormentor of enemies and enemy of Drona, with sharp arrows.

verses.text:
तस्य कर्णो महाराज शरं कनकभूषणम् ।
प्रेषयामास संक्रुद्धो मृत्युदण्डमिवापरम् ॥

meaning.en: Great king, Karna, angry, sent at him an arrow adorned with gold, like a second rod of Death.

verses.text:
तमापतन्तं सहसा घोररूपं विशां पते ।
चिच्छेद सप्तधा राजञ्शैनेयः कृतहस्तवत् ॥

meaning.en: Lord of the people, Satyaki, the Shaineya, with a skilled hand, cut into seven pieces that fearsome arrow as it suddenly rushed on.

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वा विनिहितं बाणं शरैः कर्णो विशां पते ।
सात्यकिं शरवर्षेण समन्तात्पर्यवारयत् ॥

meaning.en: Lord of the people, seeing his arrow cut down by arrows, Karna surrounded Satyaki on every side with a shower of arrows.

verses.text:
विव्याध चैनं समरे नाराचैस्तत्र सप्तभिः ।
तं प्रत्यविध्यच्छैनेयः शरैर्हेमविभूषितैः ॥

meaning.en: He pierced him there in the battle with seven iron arrows, and the Shaineya pierced him back with arrows adorned with gold.

verses.text:
ततो युद्धमतीवासीच्चक्षुःश्रोत्रभयावहम् ।
राजन्घोरं च चित्रं च प्रेक्षणीयं समन्ततः ॥

meaning.en: Then a battle took place that was fearful to eye and ear, king, terrible, strange and worth watching from every side.

verses.text:
सर्वेषां तत्र भूतानां लोमहर्षो व्यजायत ।
तद्दृष्ट्वा समरे कर्म कर्णशैनेययोर्नृप ॥

meaning.en: Seeing that exploit of Karna and Satyaki in the battle, king, a thrill of wonder ran through all beings there.

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे द्रौणिरभ्ययात्सुमहाबलम् ।
पार्षतं शत्रुदमनं शत्रुवीर्यासुनाशनम् ॥

meaning.en: In the meantime Ashvatthama went against the very mighty son of Prishata, tamer of foes and destroyer of enemy strength and lives.

verses.text:
अभ्यभाषत संक्रुद्धो द्रौणिर्दूरे धनंजये ।
तिष्ठ तिष्ठाद्य ब्रह्मघ्न न मे जीवन्विमोक्ष्यसे ॥

meaning.en: With Arjuna far away, Ashvatthama, enraged, said to him: "Stand, stand today, you killer of a brahmin! You will not escape me alive."

verses.text:
इत्युक्त्वा सुभृशं वीरः शीघ्रकृन्निशितैः शरैः ।
पार्षतं छादयामास घोररूपैः सुतेजनैः ।
यतमानं परं शक्त्या यतमानो महारथः ॥

meaning.en: Having said this, the hero, quick of hand, covered the son of Prishata with sharp, fierce-looking, very bright arrows; that great chariot-warrior strove with all his strength against one who was striving too.

verses.text:
यथा हि समरे द्रौणिः पार्षतं वीक्ष्य मारिष ।
तथा द्रौणिं रणे दृष्ट्वा पार्षतः परवीरहा ।
नातिहृष्टमना भूत्वा मन्यते मृत्युमात्मनः ॥

meaning.en: Lord, just as Ashvatthama looked at Dhrishtadyumna in the battle, so Dhrishtadyumna, destroyer of enemy heroes, seeing Ashvatthama in the battle, felt no great joy and thought his own death was near.

verses.text:
द्रौणिस्तु दृष्ट्वा राजेन्द्र धृष्टद्युम्नं रणे स्थितम् ।
क्रोधेन निःश्वसन्वीरः पार्षतं समुपाद्रवत् ।
तावन्योन्यं तु दृष्ट्वैव संरम्भं जग्मतुः परम् ॥

meaning.en: King of kings, Ashvatthama, seeing Dhrishtadyumna standing in the battle, sighing with anger, rushed at the son of Prishata, and the two, just from seeing each other, grew greatly furious.

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीन्महाराज द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान् ।
धृष्टद्युम्नं समीपस्थं त्वरमाणो विशां पते ।
पाञ्चालापसदाद्य त्वां प्रेषयिष्यामि मृत्यवे ॥

meaning.en: Then, great king, mighty Ashvatthama, hurrying, said to Dhrishtadyumna, who was close by: "You wretch of the Panchalas, today I shall send you to your death.

verses.text:
पापं हि यत्त्वया कर्म घ्नता द्रोणं पुरा कृतम् ।
अद्य त्वा पत्स्यते तद्वै यथा ह्यकुशलं तथा ॥

meaning.en: The sinful deed you did before in killing Drona will fall on you today, as surely as an unlucky outcome.

verses.text:
अरक्ष्यमाणः पार्थेन यदि तिष्ठसि संयुगे ।
नापक्रमसि वा मूढ सत्यमेतद्ब्रवीमि ते ॥

meaning.en: If you stand in the battle unprotected by Arjuna, and do not run away, fool, I tell you this truly."

verses.text:
एवमुक्तः प्रत्युवाच धृष्टद्युम्नः प्रतापवान् ।
प्रतिवाक्यं स एवासिर्मामको दास्यते तव ।
येनैव ते पितुर्दत्तं यतमानस्य संयुगे ॥

meaning.en: Spoken to thus, mighty Dhrishtadyumna replied: "My sword itself will give you the answer, the same sword that was given to your father as he struggled in the battle.

verses.text:
यदि तावन्मया द्रोणो निहतो ब्राह्मणब्रुवः ।
त्वामिदानीं कथं युद्धे न हनिष्यामि विक्रमात् ॥

meaning.en: If I have killed Drona, that brahmin in name only, why should I not now kill you in the battle by my valour?"

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाराज सेनापतिरमर्षणः ।
निशितेनाथ बाणेन द्रौणिं विव्याध पार्षतः ॥

meaning.en: Having said this, great king, the angry commander, the son of Prishata, pierced Ashvatthama with a sharp arrow.

verses.text:
ततो द्रौणिः सुसंक्रुद्धः शरैः संनतपर्वभिः ।
प्राच्छादयद्दिशो राजन्धृष्टद्युम्नस्य संयुगे ॥

meaning.en: Then Ashvatthama, very angry, covered the directions around Dhrishtadyumna in the battle with arrows with bent joints.

verses.text:
नैवान्तरिक्षं न दिशो नैव योधाः समन्ततः ।
दृश्यन्ते वै महाराज शरैश्छन्नाः सहस्रशः ॥

meaning.en: Great king, neither the sky nor the directions nor the warriors on every side could be seen, covered by thousands of arrows.

verses.text:
तथैव पार्षतो राजन्द्रौणिमाहवशोभिनम् ।
शरैः संछादयामास सूतपुत्रस्य पश्यतः ॥

meaning.en: In the same way, king, the son of Prishata covered Ashvatthama, shining in the battle, with arrows, while Karna looked on.

verses.text:
राधेयोऽपि महाराज पाञ्चालान्सह पाण्डवैः ।
द्रौपदेयान्युधामन्युं सात्यकिं च महारथम् ।
एकः स वारयामास प्रेक्षणीयः समन्ततः ॥

meaning.en: Great king, Radheya too, a sight worth seeing, alone held back on every side the Panchalas with the Pandavas, the sons of Draupadi, Yudhamanyu and the great chariot-warrior Satyaki.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नोऽपि समरे द्रौणेश्चिच्छेद कार्मुकम् ।
तदपास्य धनुश्छिन्नमन्यदादत्त कार्मुकम् ।
वेगवत्समरे घोरं शरांश्चाशीविषोपमान् ॥

meaning.en: In the battle Dhrishtadyumna cut Ashvatthama's bow; throwing aside the cut bow, Ashvatthama took another, and swiftly, fiercely in the battle, took arrows like venomous snakes.

verses.text:
स पार्षतस्य राजेन्द्र धनुः शक्तिं गदां ध्वजम् ।
हयान्सूतं रथं चैव निमेषाद्व्यधमच्छरैः ॥

meaning.en: Lord of kings, in an instant he destroyed with arrows the son of Prishata's bow, spear, mace, banner, horses, charioteer and chariot.

verses.text:
स छिन्नधन्वा विरथो हताश्वो हतसारथिः ।
खड्गमादत्त विपुलं शतचन्द्रं च भानुमत् ॥

meaning.en: With bow cut, chariotless, horses slain and charioteer slain, Dhrishtadyumna took up a broad, shining sword and a shield marked with a hundred moons.

verses.text:
द्रौणिस्तदपि राजेन्द्र भल्लैः क्षिप्रं महारथः ।
चिच्छेद समरे वीरः क्षिप्रहस्तो दृढायुधः ।
रथादनवरूढस्य तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥

meaning.en: Lord of kings, Ashvatthama, the great chariot-warrior, quick of hand and firm in his weapons, swiftly cut that too with broad-headed arrows in the battle; and it was a marvel, as Dhrishtadyumna had not got down from his chariot.

verses.text:
धृष्टद्युम्नं तु विरथं हताश्वं छिन्नकार्मुकम् ।
शरैश्च बहुधा विद्धमस्त्रैश्च शकलीकृतम् ।
नातरद्भरतश्रेष्ठ यतमानो महारथः ॥

meaning.en: Best of the Bharatas, Dhrishtadyumna, chariotless, horses slain, bow cut, pierced many times by arrows and shattered by weapons, though that great chariot-warrior strove, could not get free.

verses.text:
तस्यान्तमिषुभी राजन्यदा द्रौणिर्न जग्मिवान् ।
अथ त्यक्त्वा धनुर्वीरः पार्षतं त्वरितोऽन्वगात् ॥

meaning.en: King, when Ashvatthama had not reached his end with arrows, the hero threw down his bow and quickly went after the son of Prishata.

verses.text:
आसीदाद्रवतो राजन्वेगस्तस्य महात्मनः ।
गरुडस्येव पततो जिघृक्षोः पन्नगोत्तमम् ॥

meaning.en: King, as that great-souled man ran on, his speed was like that of Garuda as he swoops, eager to seize the best of snakes.

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु माधवोऽर्जुनमब्रवीत् ।
पश्य पार्थ यथा द्रौणिः पार्षतस्य वधं प्रति ।
यत्नं करोति विपुलं हन्याच्चैनमसंशयम् ॥

meaning.en: At that very time Madhava said to Arjuna: "Look, Arjuna, how Ashvatthama is making a great effort to kill the son of Prishata; without doubt he would kill him.

verses.text:
तं मोचय महाबाहो पार्षतं शत्रुतापनम् ।
द्रौणेरास्यमनुप्राप्तं मृत्योरास्यगतं यथा ॥

meaning.en: Mighty-armed one, free that scorcher of enemies, the son of Prishata, who has come into Ashvatthama's mouth, like one who has gone into the mouth of death."

verses.text:
एवमुक्त्वा महाराज वासुदेवः प्रतापवान् ।
प्रैषयत्तत्र तुरगान्यत्र द्रौणिर्व्यवस्थितः ॥

meaning.en: Having said this, great king, the mighty Vasudeva sent the horses to where Ashvatthama stood.

verses.text:
ते हयाश्चन्द्रसंकाशाः केशवेन प्रचोदिताः ।
पिबन्त इव तद्व्योम जग्मुर्द्रौणिरथं प्रति ॥

meaning.en: Those horses, moon-white, urged on by Keshava, went to Ashvatthama's chariot as if drinking the sky.

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वायान्तौ महावीर्यावुभौ कृष्णधनंजयौ ।
धृष्टद्युम्नवधे राजंश्चक्रे यत्नं महाबलः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing those two of great prowess, Krishna and Arjuna, coming, mighty Ashvatthama made an effort to kill Dhrishtadyumna.

verses.text:
विकृष्यमाणं दृष्ट्वैव धृष्टद्युम्नं जनेश्वर ।
शरांश्चिक्षेप वै पार्थो द्रौणिं प्रति महाबलः ॥

meaning.en: Lord of men, seeing Dhrishtadyumna being dragged away, mighty Arjuna, son of Pritha, shot arrows at Ashvatthama.

verses.text:
ते शरा हेमविकृता गाण्डीवप्रेषिता भृशम् ।
द्रौणिमासाद्य विविशुर्वल्मीकमिव पन्नगाः ॥

meaning.en: Those golden arrows, sent forcibly from the Gandiva, reached Ashvatthama and entered him like snakes into an anthill.

verses.text:
स विध्वस्तैः शरैर्घोरैर्द्रोणपुत्रः प्रतापवान् ।
रथमारुरुहे वीरो धनंजयशरार्दितः ।
प्रगृह्य च धनुः श्रेष्ठं पार्थं विव्याध सायकैः ॥

meaning.en: The mighty hero, Drona's son, tormented by Arjuna's arrows, scattered by those fearsome shafts, climbed into his chariot, took up his best bow and wounded Arjuna with arrows.

verses.text:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे वीरः सहदेवो जनाधिप ।
अपोवाह रथेनाजौ पार्षतं शत्रुतापनम् ॥

meaning.en: In the meantime, lord of the people, the hero Sahadeva carried the son of Prishata, tormentor of enemies, off the field on his chariot.

verses.text:
अर्जुनोऽपि महाराज द्रौणिं विव्याध पत्रिभिः ।
तं द्रोणपुत्रः संक्रुद्धो बाह्वोरुरसि चार्दयत् ॥

meaning.en: Great king, Arjuna too pierced Ashvatthama with arrows, and angry Ashvatthama struck him in the arms and chest.

verses.text:
क्रोधितस्तु रणे पार्थो नाराचं कालसंमितम् ।
द्रोणपुत्राय चिक्षेप कालदण्डमिवापरम् ।
स ब्राह्मणस्यांसदेशे निपपात महाद्युतिः ॥

meaning.en: Enraged in the battle, Arjuna hurled at Ashvatthama an iron arrow like Time itself, like a second rod of Death, and that very bright arrow fell on the brahmin's shoulder.

verses.text:
स विह्वलो महाराज शरवेगेन संयुगे ।
निषसाद रथोपस्थे वैक्लव्यं च परं ययौ ॥

meaning.en: Great king, shaken by the force of the arrow in the battle, he sank down on the seat of his chariot and fell into great distress.

verses.text:
ततः कर्णो महाराज व्याक्षिपद्विजयं धनुः ।
अर्जुनं समरे क्रुद्धः प्रेक्षमाणो मुहुर्मुहुः ।
द्वैरथं चापि पार्थेन कामयानो महारणे ॥

meaning.en: Then, great king, Karna in anger twanged his bow Vijaya, looking at Arjuna again and again, wishing for a duel of chariots with the son of Pritha in the great battle.

verses.text:
तं तु हित्वा हतं वीरं सारथिः शत्रुकर्शनम् ।
अपोवाह रथेनाजौ त्वरमाणो रणाजिरात् ॥

meaning.en: Then Ashvatthama's charioteer, hurrying, carried that scorcher of enemies, thought slain, out of the battlefield on the chariot.

verses.text:
अथोत्क्रुष्टं महाराज पाञ्चालैर्जितकाशिभिः ।
मोक्षितं पार्षतं दृष्ट्वा द्रोणपुत्रं च पीडितम् ॥

meaning.en: Then, great king, the Panchalas, victorious with the Kashis, raised a shout on seeing Dhrishtadyumna freed and Ashvatthama hurt.

verses.text:
वादित्राणि च दिव्यानि प्रावाद्यन्त सहस्रशः ।
सिंहनादश्च संजज्ञे दृष्ट्वा घोरं महाद्भुतम् ॥

meaning.en: Thousands of divine instruments were played, and a lion-roar arose as they saw that fearful, very marvellous deed.

verses.text:
एवं कृत्वाब्रवीत्पार्थो वासुदेवं धनंजयः ।
याहि संशप्तकान्कृष्ण कार्यमेतत्परं मम ॥

meaning.en: Having done this, Arjuna, son of Pritha, said to Vasudeva: "Krishna, go to the Samshaptakas; this is my main task."

verses.text:
ततः प्रयातो दाशार्हः श्रुत्वा पाण्डवभाषितम् ।
रथेनातिपताकेन मनोमारुतरंहसा ॥

meaning.en: Then Krishna, descendant of Dasharha, hearing what the Pandava said, went forth on his chariot with many banners, swift as mind and wind.
